questions.question: Explain why the ancient Egyptians built the pyramids.
questions.expected_answer: They believed in an afterlife, where a person's spirit lived on. The body had to be preserved and placed in a safe tomb with everything needed for the afterlife. Pharaohs, as god-kings, needed the grandest tombs, so pyramids were built as their tombs, from Djoser's Step Pyramid to Khufu's Great Pyramid at Giza.

questions.question: Describe how the pyramids were built and who built them.
questions.expected_answer: Stone was cut with copper chisels, stone hammers and wooden wedges, carried on Nile boats, and dragged on sledges over wet sand. Ramps were probably used to raise the blocks, and the work took many years. A workers' town with bakeries and workers' graves shows that the builders were mostly paid workers, fed and cared for, many perhaps farmers during the flood season.

questions.question: Describe the Great Sphinx and the purpose of temples.
questions.expected_answer: The Great Sphinx at Giza is a huge statue with a lion's body and a man's head wearing a royal headcloth, carved from the limestone rock, possibly showing the pharaoh Khafre, and seen as a guardian. Temples were houses of the gods, with a statue in a dark inner sanctuary where only priests could enter to care for it daily, while ordinary people prayed in the outer courts.
